steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Media contexts are the social, cultural, political, historical, and economic circumstances in which media products are produced and consumed. Context shapes meaning.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social context: the social issues and attitudes at the time of production — e.g. changing attitudes to gender, race, and sexuality are reflected in media representations.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cultural context: the shared values, beliefs, and practices of a society or group — media products both reflect and shape culture. British media has distinct cultural codes different from American.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Political context: the political environment affects media — regulation, funding, government policy, and political events all shape what media is produced and how. Public service broadcasting exists because of political decisions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
